steps.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)

evidence: Directly changes LICM's MemorySSA-based safety predicate and permits additional memory-def/call hoists.
LICM and loop-mssa occur in the relevant O3 optimization region; changed memory placement can leave a later loop transform with a different MemorySSA use graph.
Although it does not modify removeFromLookups directly, it is the strongest candidate that can introduce a new invalid memory-motion topology before SimpleLoopUnswitch.
features: dominance-check, licm, loop-mssa, memory-hoisting, memoryssa, meta:core-llvm
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes LICM's MemorySSA-based conflict check so that, during hoisting (but not sinking), memory accesses dominated by the instruction's defining MemorySSA access are skipped when checking for conflicting reads/writes. It therefore permits additional hoists where the prior check treated dominated accesses as potential conflicts. The accompanying LICM tests establish both a newly permitted hoist of an inaccessible-memory-writing call and cases that must remain unhoisted when inaccessible memory conflicts.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA::dominates; LICM; loop_alias; ne_loop_alias
Behavioral change: For hoisting, noConflictingReadWrites now ignores an access MA when the instruction's MemoryDef IMD dominates MA.; LICM may hoist more memory-writing instructions or calls because dominated MemorySSA accesses no longer block the hoist-safety decision.; The change is restricted by !Flags.getIsSink(), so sinking retains the prior conflict-check behavior.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses; MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run
Reproducer link: The failure occurs at -O3 in a pipeline containing loop-mssa, licm, and simple-loop-unswitch.; This commit changes LICM's MemorySSA-driven memory-motion decisions, which can alter the MemorySSA graph and loop IR subsequently seen by SimpleLoopUnswitch.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; loop-mssa; MemorySSA; MemorySSAUpdater; SimpleLoopUnswitch
Causal explanation: The commit directly modifies a MemorySSA-based LICM safety predicate in a pass present in the failing -O3 pipeline. Permitting an extra hoist changes memory-access placement and can create a different MemorySSA/use topology for later loop transformations, including the crashing SimpleLoopUnswitch removal path. However, the retrieved hunk neither changes MemorySSAUpdater/removeBlocks nor demonstrates the reported assertion, and the observed failing frame is in SimpleLoopUnswitch rather than LICM. The link is therefore plausible but indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.40
Build risk: Implementation change is confined to llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LICM.cpp and has dedicated LICM regression coverage.; New test file runs opt -passes='loop-mssa(licm)', directly exercising the changed MemorySSA-backed LICM path.; Existing invariant.start LICM output checks were updated, indicating the safety-rule change intentionally changes optimized IR.; No retrieved test reproduces MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks or the removeFromLookups assertion.

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..03ab270de12e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(licm)' < %s -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; It should hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; because there is no conflict between inaccessible memory
+;; fn_read_inaccessible_mem is a nice side effect
+define i32 @loop_alias(i64 %x, ptr %start) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @loop_alias(
+; CHECK-SAME: i64 [[X:%.*]], ptr [[START:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[START]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[GEP:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOAD:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[PHI]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_args(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_args(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %load)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x
+  %acc = add nuw nsw i32 %val, 1
+  %cmp = icmp ult i32 %acc, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %after_loop
+after_loop:
+  ret i32 %acc
+}
+
+;; It should NOT hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; Because fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2 reads the same inaccessible memory
+define i32 @ne_loop_alias(i64 %x, ptr %start) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @ne_loop_alias(
+; CHECK-SAME: i64 [[X:%.*]], ptr [[START:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[START]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[GEP:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOAD:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[PHI]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[VAL]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %val)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x
+  %acc = add nuw nsw i32 %val, 1
+  %cmp = icmp ult i32 %acc, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %after_loop
+after_loop:
+  ret i32 %acc
+}
+
+;; Should hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; It does not alias with store
+define void @hoist_untill_I(ptr noalias %loc, ptr noalias %loc2){
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @hoist_untill_I(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr noalias [[LOC:%.*]], ptr noalias [[LOC2:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[LOC2]], align 4
+; CHECK-N

top_candidates.subject: Revert [LICM] Remove unnecessary check during store hoisting (#195606)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit restores a conservative LICM hoist-safety condition in noConflictingReadWrites. When considering hoisting, LICM now rejects the transformation if an optimized MemorySSA use MU is not dominated by the instruction's MemoryDef IMD. The code comments explain that optimized uses may refer to an access outside the loop because getClobbering can walk the loop backedge to a previous iteration. The added regression test covers a load before a store where an out-of-loop liveOnEntry clobber would otherwise make a store hoist appear safe.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA::dominates; getClobbering; LICM; load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def; loop_alias
Behavioral change: LICM hoisting now fails when an optimized MemorySSA use is not dominated by the candidate instruction's MemoryDef.; The restored guard prevents hoists across potentially interfering loads even if the load's clobbering access is outside the loop.; The change deliberately trades away some hoisting opportunities, including the inaccessible-memory-call case marked FIXME, for conservative correctness.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses; MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run
Reproducer link: The -O3 failure pipeline includes loop-mssa, licm, and simple-loop-unswitch.; The new test specifically models loop backedge MemorySSA behavior in which an optimized use can have a liveOnEntry/out-of-loop clobber despite a potentially interfering in-loop load.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; loop-mssa; MemorySSA; MemorySSAUpdater; SimpleLoopUnswitch
Causal explanation: This is strong subsystem-level evidence because it restores a MemorySSA dominance invariant used to decide whether LICM may move a store or memory-writing operation across a load. Such movement can affect the later loop shape and MemorySSA use graph that SimpleLoopUnswitch updates before the reported removeFromLookups assertion. The new test proves a previously accepted hoist was invalid under backedge-aware clobbering. Still, the retrieved evidence does not show that this particular assertion is triggered by the bad hoist, nor does it modify the updater code that asserts; it is best characterized as a plausible protective/fix candidate rather than proven direct cause.
Causal confidence: 0.53
Build risk: The implementation change is small and localized to LICM's MemorySSA conflict check.; A focused regression test, load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def, documents and tests the restored conservative behavior.; Several LICM expected-output tests change because fewer hoists are performed.; No retrieved test invokes SimpleLoopUnswitch or directly validates absence of MemorySSA::removeFromLookups assertions.

@@ -691,0 +692,35 @@ exit:
+
+@g1 = external global i8
+@g2 = external global i8
+
+; The store should not be hoisted here, because the location is accessed by the
+; preceding load. However, the clobbering memory access for that load is
+; liveOnEntry, because the pointer on the backedge does not alias. As such,
+; only checking whether the clobbering access is outside the loop is
+; insufficient.
+define i8 @load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def(i1 %c) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i8 @load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[C:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ @g1, %[[ENTRY]] ], [ @g2, %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = load i8, ptr [[PHI]], align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i8 1, ptr @g1, align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[V]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i8 [[V_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ @g1, %entry ], [ @g2, %loop ]

top_candidates.subject: [GVN] MemorySSA for GVN: eliminate redundant loads via MemorySSA (#152859)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit substantially extends GVN's optional MemorySSA mode for redundant-load elimination. It adds MemorySSA-based reaching-memory-value discovery, including scanning MemoryAccess users in a block with alias and dominance checks, adds helpers for load/store and masked-memory locations, preserves the older MemDep path when MemorySSA is disabled, and updates GVN/PRE expectations to converge the MemDep and MemorySSA results.

causal_evidence.summary: This commit substantially extends GVN's optional MemorySSA mode for redundant-load elimination. It adds MemorySSA-based reaching-memory-value discovery, including scanning MemoryAccess users in a block with alias and dominance checks, adds helpers for load/store and masked-memory locations, preserves the older MemDep path when MemorySSA is disabled, and updates GVN/PRE expectations to converge the MemDep and MemorySSA results.

Summary: This commit adds opt-in SROA canonicalization of eligible tightly packed homogeneous struct partitions to fixed-vector types, then enables that option for a later SROA invocation in the optimization pipeline after MemCpyOpt. The new helper accepts only same-element integer, floating-point, or integral-pointer structs with equal struct/vector allocation size and partitions whose non-debug/non-lifetime users are memory intrinsics. The resulting vector representation can permit alloca promotion and changes the load/store and memcpy shapes seen by later optimization passes.
Changed symbols: llvm::SROAPass::run; SROA::selectPartitionType; SROA::presplitLoadsAndStores; tryCanonicalizeStructToVector; SROAOptions::AggregateToVector; llvm::PassBuilder::addVectorPasses; store_only_fp_tail; move_then_swap
Behavioral change: SROA can replace a homogeneous, tightly packed struct partition with a FixedVectorType when AggregateToVector is enabled and the partition is used only by memory intrinsics apart from lifetime/debug users.; This changes eligible memory copies from aggregate-oriented handling to vector loads, inserts, and stores, and can enable promotion of vector allocas to SSA values.; The default O3 pipeline gains an SROA pass with AggregateToVector enabled after MemCpyOpt, explicitly to avoid hiding memcpy chains from MemCpyOpt when run earlier.; The added tests demonstrate altered memory IR, including a <2 x i64> load/store sequence and a <4 x float> store assembled with insertelement.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses
Reproducer link: The crash occurs under -O3, and the new PhaseOrdering test explicitly runs default<O3>.; The commit introduces new O3-reachable SROA rewriting of memcpy-heavy allocas and changes the memory-access graph available to subsequent optimization passes.; The retrieved tests do not reproduce the reported assertion or exercise MemorySSAUpdater block removal.
Pass or subsystem link: SROA; MemCpyOpt phase ordering; default<O3> pipeline; downstream scalar and loop optimizers using MemorySSA

Such altered CFG-independent memory-access structure can reach later loop passes, including the SimpleLoopUnswitch path named in the trace, where MemorySSAUpdater removes blocks. However, no retrieved hunk updates MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, SimpleLoopUnswitch, or block-deletion bookkeeping, and the visible evidence does not establish that this new SROA form leaves a MemoryAccess with uses. new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e98c9074e4f8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -S -passes='default<O3>' %s | FileCheck %s
+
+%pair = type { i64, i64 }
+%quad = type { i64, i64, i64, i64 }
+
+declare void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr noalias writeonly captures(none), ptr noalias readonly captures(none), i64, i1 immarg)
+declare void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr writeonly captures(none), i8, i64, i1 immarg)
+
+; This test verifies that the default O3 pipeline canonicalizes struct allocas
+; to vectors only after memcpyopt has run. The input pattern is:
+;
+;   memcpy tmp, obj, 16
+;   memset obj + 16, 0, 16
+;
+;  ----- SWAP(other, tmp) -----
+;
+;   memcpy swap.tmp, tmp, 16
+;   memcpy tmp, other, 16
+;   memcpy other, swap.tmp, 16
+;
+; It swaps the first 16-bytes of other and tmp, but the first 16-bytes of tmp
+; are the same as the first 16-bytes of obj. This comes from real code from
+; DuckDB, where the swap function is inlined. If struct-to-vector canonicalization
+; runs before memcpyopt, swap.tmp gets promoted to an SSA value and we are stuck
+; saving tmp to swap.tmp. Delaying canonicalization until after memcpyopt lets
+; memcpyopt notice that tmp and obj share the same first 16-bytes, so swap.tmp
+; is no longer needed and the IR collapses to a single load/memmove/store.
+define void @move_then_swap(ptr %dst, ptr %src, ptr %other) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @move_then_swap(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr writeonly captures(none) initializes((0, 16)) [[DST:%.*]], ptr readonly captures(none) [[SRC:%.*]], ptr captures(none) [[OTHER:%.*]]) local_unnamed_addr #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD:%.*]] = load <2 x i64>, ptr [[OTHER]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    tail call void @llvm.memmove.p0.p0.i64(ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[OTHER]], ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[SRC]], i64 16, i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store <2 x i64> [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD]], ptr [[DST]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  %obj = alloca %quad, align 8
+  %swap.tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj, ptr align 8 %src, i64 32, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %obj, i64 16, i1 false)
+  %obj.tail = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %obj, i64 16
+  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj.tail, i8 0, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %other, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %other, ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

+; patterns for clarity.
+
+; When SROA splits { ptr, i64, i64, i64 } into [0,8), [8,16), [16,32),
+; the [16,32) partition type from getTypePartition is { i64, i64 }.
+; With the simplified fallback rule, that partition canonicalizes to <2 x i64>
+; because its remaining users are all mem intrinsics.
+
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @test_subpartition_type(
+; CHECK: %a.sroa.6.0.copyload = load <2 x i64>, ptr %a.sroa.6.0.src.sroa_idx, align 8
+; CHECK: store <2 x i64> %a.sroa.6.0.copyload, ptr %a.sroa.6.0.dst.sroa_idx, align 8
+define void @test_subpartition_type(ptr %src, ptr %dst) {
+entry:
+  %a = alloca { ptr, i64, i64, i64 }, align 8
+  call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(i64 32, ptr %a)
+
+  ; Copy all 32 bytes from src into %a (splittable)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %a, ptr align 8 %src, i64 32, i1 false)
+
+  ; Load ptr at [0,8) -- forces partition boundary at 8
+  %p = load ptr, ptr %a, align 8
+
+  ; Load i64 at [8,16) -- forces partition boundary at 16
+  %gep.a.8 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %a, i64 8
+  %v1 = load i64, ptr %gep.a.8, align 8
+
+  ; Only splittable memcpy uses touch [16,32), so SROA creates a single
+  ; [16,32) partition. getTypePartition returns { i64, i64 } for this, and
+  ; the simplified fallback rule canonicalizes it to <2 x i64>.
+
+  ; Copy all 32 bytes from %a to dst (splittable)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %a, i64 32, i1 false)
+
+  call void @llvm.lifetime.end.p0(i64 32, ptr %a)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; Element-wise { double, double } access through a phi.
+; The phi between two allocas prevents SROA slice analysis
+; ("A pointer to this alloca escaped"), so the allocas survive.
+
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @test_elementwise_phi(
+; CHECK-NOT: <2 x double>
+define void @test_elementwise_phi(ptr %src0, ptr %src1, i1 %cond, ptr %dst) {
+entry:
+  %a = alloca { double, double }, align 8
+  %b = alloca { double, double }, align 8
+  %a.1 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %a, i64 8
+  %b.1 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %b, i64 8
+  %v0 = load double, ptr %src0, align 8
+  %v1 = load double, ptr %src1, align 8
+  store double %v0, ptr %a, align 8
+  store double %v1, ptr %a.1, align 8
+  store double 0.0, ptr %b, align 8
+  store double 0.0, ptr %b.1, align 8
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  br label %merge
+
+if.else:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %sel = phi ptr [ %a, %if.then ], [ %b, %if.else ]
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %sel, i64 16, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

Summary: This commit enables loop vectorization of uncountable early-exit loops that contain stores by deriving an early-exit lane mask and applying it to vectorized memory operations. It restructures VPlan early-exit handling to disconnect early-exiting VPlan blocks, remove associated terminators and phi incoming values, derive the exit condition, and build masked load/store vectorization plans; it also adds coverage for interleaving, tail folding, scalarized conditional operations, and target-specific cases.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::handleUncountableEarlyExits; handleUncountableExitsWithSideEffects; EarlyExitInfo; VPlanTransforms::convertToConcreteRecipes; loop_contains_store_condition_load_has_single_user; loop_contains_store_after_uncountable_exit

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit changes Loop Strength Reduction handling of pointer-typed ICmpZero uses. LSRInstance::Expand converts the expansion type to ScalarEvolution's effective integer SCEV type for pointer comparisons, and LSRInstance::Rewrite suppresses the otherwise-required cast back to the pointer operand type. The resulting transformed IR compares integer induction values/bounds directly and avoids generating inttoptr casts; tests are updated and added to require that result.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::Expand; LSRInstance::Rewrite; LSRUse::ICmpZero; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll; b_copy_ctor test expectations in pr27056.ll; LoopStrengthReduce test expectations in pr25541.ll
Behavioral change: For pointer-typed ICmpZero uses, LSR expands operands in the integer domain by setting OpTy to SE.getEffectiveSCEVType(OpTy).; During rewrite, pointer-typed ICmpZero values are not cast back when the expanded integer value type differs from the original pointer type.; LSR therefore emits integer comparisons such as icmp eq i64 induction-value, 0 instead of materializing an inttoptr and comparing pointers.; The added X86 test verifies an integer induction variable and integer exit comparisons while retaining the loop's loads and store through GEP-derived pointers.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses; SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O3 crash while updating MemorySSA.; This commit's tests invoke -passes=loop-reduce, not clang -O3 and not the reported MemorySSAUpdater/removeBlocks failure path.; The updated tests include loops with pointer IVs, loads, and a store, but do not demonstrate the reported assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce; ScalarEvolution; MemorySSA/MemorySSAUpdater failure path; SimpleLoopUnswitch
Causal explanation: The change can alter the IR supplied to later optimization passes by replacing pointer/inttoptr-based ICmpZero handling with integer-domain comparisons. That makes it a plausible indirect scalar-pipeline interaction candidate for later MemorySSA users. However, the retrieved hunks do not modify MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, CFG/block removal, or SimpleLoopUnswitch, and the crash trace identifies SimpleLoopUnswitch's removeBlocks path rather than LSR. The evidence therefore supports only a weak, indirect link.
Causal confidence: 0.08

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..0d6a374f8669
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-reduce -S %s | FileCheck %s
+;
+; Verify that LSR keeps ICmpZero comparisons in the integer domain when the
+; original operands are pointers, avoiding inttoptr casts entirely. The loop
+; has three pointer IVs sharing the same stride; LSR should produce a single
+; integer IV and compare it directly against the precomputed bound.
+; Target-dependent because TTI must report that scaled addressing is legal.
+
+target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
+target datalayout = "e-m:e-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
+
+define void @test_no_inttoptr_casts(ptr %base1, ptr %base2, ptr %base3, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @test_no_inttoptr_casts(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = shl i64 [[N:%.*]], 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ], [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE1:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP1:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE2:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP2:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE3:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_EXIT:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_EXIT]], label [[CHECK:%.*]], label [[BODY:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       check:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP3:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i1 true, i1 [[CMP3]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[SEL]], label [[BODY]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       body:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V1:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V2:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP1]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUM:%.*]] = add i64 [[V1]], [[V2]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SUM]], ptr [[SCEVGEP2]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %bound1 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base1, i64 %n
+  %bound2 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base2, i64 %n
+  %bound3 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base3, i64 %n
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %p1 = phi ptr [ %base1, %entry ], [ %p1.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p2 = phi ptr [ %base2, %entry ], [ %p2.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p3 = phi ptr [ %base3, %entry ], [ %p3.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %cmp.exit = icmp eq ptr %p2, %bound2
+  br i1 %cmp.exit, label %check, label %body
+
+check:
+  %cmp1 = icmp ne ptr %p1, %bound1
+  %cmp3 = icmp ne ptr %p3, %bound3
+  %sel = select i1 %cmp1, i1 true, i1 %cmp3
+  br i1 %sel, label %body, label %exit
+
+body:
+  %v1 = load i64, ptr %p1, align 8
+  %v2 = load i64, ptr %p2, align 8
+  %sum = add i64 %v1, %v2
+  store i64 %sum, ptr %p3, align 8
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+loop.latch:
+  %p1.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p1, i64 8
+  %p2.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p2, i64 8
+  %p3.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p3, i64 8
+  br label %loop
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-reduce -S %s | FileCheck %s
+;
+; Verify that LSR keeps ICmpZero comparisons in the integer domain when the
+; original operands are pointers, avoiding inttoptr casts entirely. The loop
+; has three pointer IVs sharing the same stride; LSR should produce a single
+; integer IV and compare it directly against the precomputed bound.
+; Target-dependent because TTI must report that scaled addressing is legal.
+
+target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
+target datalayout = "e-m:e-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
+
+define void @test_no_inttoptr_casts(ptr %base1, ptr %base2, ptr %base3, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @test_no_inttoptr_casts(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = shl i64 [[N:%.*]], 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ], [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE1:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP1:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE2:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP2:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE3:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_EXIT:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_EXIT]], label [[CHECK:%.*]], label [[BODY:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       check:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP3:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i1 true, i1 [[CMP3]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[SEL]], label [[BODY]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       body:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V1:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V2:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP1]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUM:%.*]] = add i64 [[V1]], [[V2]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SUM]], ptr [[SCEVGEP2]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %bound1 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base1, i64 %n
+  %bound2 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base2, i64 %n
+  %bound3 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base3, i64 %n
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %p1 = phi ptr [ %base1, %entry ], [ %p1.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p2 = phi ptr [ %base2, %entry ], [ %p2.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p3 = phi ptr [ %base3, %entry ], [ %p3.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %cmp.exit = icmp eq ptr %p2, %bound2
+  br i1 %cmp.exit, label %check, label %body
+
+check:
+  %cmp1 = icmp ne ptr %p1, %bound1
+  %cmp3 = icmp ne ptr %p3, %bound3
+  %sel = select i1 %cmp1, i1 true, i1 %cmp3
+  br i1 %sel, label %body, label %exit
+
+body:
+  %v1 = load i64, ptr %p1, align 8
+  %v2 = load i64, ptr %p2, align 8
+  %sum = add i64 %v1, %v2
+  store i64 %sum, ptr %p3, align 8
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+loop.latch:
+  %p1.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p1, i64 8
+  %p2.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p2, i64 8
+  %p3.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p3, i64 8
+  br label %loop
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

diff --git a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
index 28eef9c2790d..b2e3bbe516ed 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
@@ -827,3 +827,18 @@ bool LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested(Loop *OuterLoop, Loop *InnerLoop) {
-  // A perfectly nested loop will not have any branch in between the outer and
-  // inner block i.e. outer header will branch to either inner preheader and
-  // outerloop latch.
+  // In a perfectly nested loop the outer header branches only into the inner
+  // loop. If it can also reach the outer latch, it conditionally guards the
+  // inner loop (an imperfect nest), so the inner loop runs on only a subset of
+  // the outer iterations. Interchanging such a nest would run the inner loop on
+  // every outer iteration, including the guarded-off ones, which is illegal
+  // when the inner loop relies on the guard to terminate (e.g. an eq/ne exit
+  // whose trip count is degenerate once the guard is false). Reject by allowing
+  // the outer header to branch only into the inner loop.
+  //
+  // TODO: This is conservative. A guarded nest is still safe to interchange
+  // when the inner loop has a computable trip count that is empty exactly when
+  // the guard is false, e.g.:
+  //   for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
+  //     if (M > 0)                  // loop-invariant guard
+  //       for (j = 0; j < M; j++)   // empty when M <= 0
+  //         A[j][i] = ...;
+  // Interchanging is legal here because the inner loop runs zero times on the
+  // guarded-off iterations.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..681dca5bbcba
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes=loop-interchange \
+; RUN:     -loop-interchange-profitabilities=ignore \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-missed='loop-interchange' -disable-output \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-output=%t
+; RUN: FileCheck -input-file=%t %s
+
+; The middle loop %for.j guards the inner loop %for.k: %for.k runs only when
+; %i != 0 (the outer loop's IV), and its exit %k.next == %i is only well-defined
+; under that guard. Interchanging %for.j and %for.k would run %for.k on every
+; iteration and spin when %i == 0, so the pass must not interchange this nest.
+;
+; Pseudo code:
+;   for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)
+;     for (j = 0; j < 2; j++)
+;       if (i != 0)                  // guard on the outer IV
+;         for (k = 0; ; k++) {       // terminates only when i != 0
+;           y[j][i][k] = x[i][k][j] + w[i][k][j];
+;           if (k + 1 == i) break;
+;         }
+
+; CHECK:      --- !Missed
+; CHECK-NEXT: Pass:            loop-interchange
+; CHECK-NEXT: Name:            NotTightlyNested
+; CHECK-NEXT: Function:        main
+
+@x = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@w = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@y = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+
+define i32 @main() {
+entry:
+  br label %for.i
+
+for.i:
+  %i = phi i32 [ %i.next, %for.i.inc ], [ 0, %entry ]
+  %i.is.zero = icmp eq i32 %i, 0
+  %xbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @x, i32 %i
+  %wbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @w, i32 %i
+  %ybase = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr @y, i32 %i
+  br label %for.j
+
+for.j:
+  %j = phi i32 [ %j.next, %for.j.inc ], [ 0, %for.i ]
+  br i1 %i.is.zero, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k.ph
+
+for.k.ph:
+  %xp = getelementptr i32, ptr %xbase, i32 %j
+  %wp = getelementptr i32, ptr %wbase, i32 %j
+  %yp = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr %ybase, i32 %j
+  br label %for.k
+
+for.k:
+  %k = phi i32 [ 0, %for.k.ph ], [ %k.next, %for.k ]
+  %xk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %xp, i32 %k
+  %xv = load i32, ptr %xk, align 4
+  %wk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %wp, i32 %k
+  %wv = load i32, ptr %wk, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %xv, %wv
+  %yk = getelementptr i32, ptr %yp, i32 %k
+  store i32 %add, ptr %yk, align 4
+  %k.next = add i32 %k, 1
+  %k.done = icmp eq i32 %k.next, %i
+  br i1 %k.done, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k
+
+for.j.inc:
+  %j.next = add i32 %j, 1
+  %j.cmp = icmp eq i32 %j, 0
+  br i1 %j.cmp, label %for.j, label %for.i.inc
+
+for.i.inc:
+  %i.next = add i32 %i, 1
+  %i.done = icmp eq i32 %i.next, 3
+  br i1 %i.done, label %exit, label %for.i
+
+exit:
+  ret i32 0
+}

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Retrieved evidence is test-only and updates AArch64 LoopVectorize expectations for a larger scalar-loop interleave factor. The checked vector loops in iv_trunc, trunc_ivs_and_store, ivs_trunc_and_ext, and replicating_load_used_as_store_addr now contain four scalarized lane computations/stores per vector-loop iteration and advance the induction index by 4 rather than 2.
Changed symbols: iv_trunc; trunc_ivs_and_store; ivs_trunc_and_ext; replicating_load_used_as_store_addr; LoopVectorize AArch64 DEFAULT checks
Behavioral change: Expected LoopVectorize output changes from an index increment of 2 to an increment of 4 for the affected AArch64 scalar-loop cases.; Expected vector-loop bodies gain additional per-lane arithmetic, trunc/zext operations, loads, and stores corresponding to the larger interleave factor.; No MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, removeBlocks, or removeFromLookups implementation change is present in the retrieved hunks.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces under clang -O3.; The retrieved tests exercise loop vectorization and memory-producing loop bodies, but do not contain the reduced C reproducer or an assertion expectation.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; AArch64 target-specific vectorization tests; MemorySSA/SimpleLoopUnswitch are in the reported failure trace but are not touched by the retrieved evidence
Causal explanation: A larger default interleave factor can materially change the number and layout of loads/stores in vectorized loops, so it could indirectly expose a later optimizer bookkeeping defect. However, the observed failure is in MemorySSA block removal during SimpleLoopUnswitch, while the retrieved change contains only AArch64 LoopVectorize test updates and no direct MemorySSA or loop-unswitch update. The available evidence therefore supports only a weak, indirect connection.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Retrieved changes are test expectation updates only.; No production-source hunk is available to verify the implementation mechanism.; Coverage omitted 58 hunks, so the retrieved evidence is incomplete for full commit attribution.; No crash-file touch is reported.

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..c0db87f1aaa6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/vplan-print-before-after.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-vectorize -disable-output  -force-vector-width=4  < %s \
+; RUN:   -vplan-print-before=simplify -vplan-print-before=printFinalVPlan \
+; RUN:   2>&1 | FileCheck %s -DBEFORE_OR_AFTER=before  --check-prefix=CHECK \
+; RUN:           --implicit-check-not "VPlan before"
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-vectorize -disable-output  -force-vector-width=4  < %s \
+; RUN:   -vplan-print-after=simplify -vplan-print-after=printFinalVPlan \
+; RUN:   2>&1 | FileCheck %s -DBEFORE_OR_AFTER=after --check-prefix=CHECK \
+; RUN:           --implicit-check-not "VPlan after"
+; REQUIRES: asserts
+
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] simplifyRecipes
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] simplifyBlends
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] simplifyRecipes
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] printFinalVPlan
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Final VPlan for VF={4},UF={1}' {
+
+define void @foo(ptr %ptr, i64 %n) {
+entry:
+  br label %header
+
+header:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %header ]
+  %gep = getelementptr i64, ptr %ptr, i64 %iv
+  store i64 %iv, ptr %gep
+  %iv.next = add nsw i64 %iv, 1
+  %exitcond = icmp slt i64 %iv.next, %n
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %header, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

steps.subject: [InstCombine] Fold X == Identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y) (#202748)

evidence: Changes an InstCombine-adjacent simplification of pure integer min/max intrinsics.
The fold has only indirect pipeline-shape effects and does not remove memory accesses or CFG blocks.
features: instcombine, instruction-simplify, meta:core-llvm, minmax-intrinsics, path:llvm/include/llvm/IR, path:llvm/lib/Analysis/InstructionSimplify.cpp
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds a general identity-value API for integer min/max intrinsics and extends instruction simplification to replace a min/max intrinsic with its non-identity operand after operand replacement. The accompanying InstCombine tests cover unsigned/signed min/max identity comparisons, operand order, negative cases, and dropping a range annotation when the intrinsic is eliminated.
Changed symbols: llvm::MinMaxIntrinsic::getIdentity(Intrinsic::ID, unsigned); llvm::MinMaxIntrinsic::getIdentity(); simplifyWithOpsReplaced; select_signed_max_smin; select_npos_umin; select_not_npos_umin; select_npos_umin_commuted; select_npos_wrong_bound_negative
Behavioral change: InstructionSimplify now recognizes integer umin/umax/smin/smax operands equal to the intrinsic identity and folds the intrinsic result to the other operand.; The fold is suppressed when poison-generating annotations cannot be dropped; when dropping is permitted, the intrinsic is recorded in DropFlags before replacement.; InstCombine test expectations show select expressions such as X == identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y) simplifying to the min/max result, including commuted umin operands.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; Trying to remove memory access that still has uses; llvm::MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; llvm::SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run
Reproducer link: The failure occurs during clang -O3 compilation.; The -O3 pipeline includes instcombine, so this change is in a pass family executed by the reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: InstructionSimplify; InstCombine; LLVM IR min/max intrinsic simplification
Causal explanation: The visible implementation change is an InstCombine-adjacent, value-only fold of pure integer min/max intrinsics; it neither touches MemorySSA nor updates/removes memory accesses or blocks. It could only affect the failure indirectly by changing simplified IR before later loop transformations. The assertion stack identifies MemorySSAUpdater block removal through SimpleLoopUnswitch rather than InstCombine, and the retrieved hunks provide no direct memory-access bookkeeping path.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Adds public MinMaxIntrinsic identity helper overloads in IntrinsicInst.h, affecting consumers of that header.; Includes focused InstCombine regression tests for the new folds.; No MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, loop-unswitch, or block-deletion implementation hunk is present.

Summary: This NFC-labelled GVN change modifies AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue so that a rematerialized SelectInst is inserted at the supplied InsertPt rather than immediately before the original select instruction. The accompanying GVN PRE test updates reflect the resulting instruction ordering changes, including select placement around loop backedges and invokes.
Changed symbols: llvm::gvn::AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue; SelectInst::Create; test_pointer_phi_select_same_object; test_pointer_phi_select_load_may_not_execute_1; test_pointer_phi_select_load_may_not_execute_2
Behavioral change: Rematerialized select values in GVN are inserted using InsertPt->getIterator() instead of Sel->getIterator().; This can change the IR location and ordering of a newly created select, while retaining the same select condition and operands.; The updated tests show changed expected placement/formatting of the generated select in loop PRE cases.
Assertion or trace link: The crash asserts in MemorySSA::removeFromLookups through MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks.; No retrieved hunk modifies MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, removeFromLookups, or block-removal logic.

Summary: This NFC test-only commit regenerates GVN checks and expands several GVN tests to run both ordinary GVN and gvn<memoryssa>. It splits expectations into MDEP and MSSA prefixes, documenting that the two GVN configurations can produce different IR in load-through-select and loop PRE cases, but it changes no optimizer implementation.
Changed symbols: GVN test RUN lines; FileCheck MDEP prefix; FileCheck MSSA prefix; test_pointer_phi_select_load_may_not_execute_1
Behavioral change: Tests now execute GVN both with its ordinary configuration and with gvn<memoryssa>.; FileCheck expectations are separated for memory-dependence-based and MemorySSA-based GVN output.; The loop PRE test records that the MemorySSA GVN variant leaves the exit load/return form rather than the MDEP expected rematerialized select form.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA is explicitly enabled by the newly added gvn<memoryssa> test invocations.; The reported assertion is MemorySSA::removeFromLookups via MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks, but this commit changes no such implementation.
Reproducer link: The updated pre-loop-load-through-select test contains loop loads, pointer selects, and a may_throw call, all relevant to memory-sensitive optimization testing.; The retrieved tests run opt directly rather than the reported reduced C testcase under clang -O3, and they do not exercise the reported SimpleLoopUnswitch failure path.
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; GVN with MemorySSA; The crash stack instead identifies MemorySSAUpdater block removal during SimpleLoopUnswitch.
Causal explanation: This commit is useful diagnostic evidence that GVN has a MemorySSA-backed mode and that its output differs from the ordinary mode on related load/select loop tests. Nevertheless, it is test-only and cannot itself introduce the MemorySSA use-list invariant violation. It could at most expose an existing regression when the added tests are run.
Causal confidence: 0.02
Build risk: Test-only NFC change; no production LLVM source is modified in the retrieved hunks.; Adds MemorySSA-mode coverage to several GVN tests, increasing the chance of detecting pre-existing GVN/MemorySSA regressions.; Regenerated check lines and distinct MDEP/MSSA prefixes may require expected-output maintenance but do not alter compiler behavior.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/scalar-steps-cost.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/scalar-steps-cost.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e98434bab7f7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/scalar-steps-cost.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+; REQUIRES: asserts
+; RUN: opt -p loop-vectorize -mtriple=arm64-apple-macosx -S -debug-only=loop-vectorize -disable-output %s 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+
+target datalayout = "e-m:o-i64:64-i128:128-n32:64-S128"
+
+define i32 @scalar_steps_all_lanes(ptr %start, ptr %end) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: LV: Checking a loop in 'scalar_steps_all_lanes'
+; CHECK: Cost of 1 for VF 2: {{.*}} = SCALAR-STEPS {{.*}}, ir<1>, {{.*}}
+; CHECK: Cost of 1 for VF 4: {{.*}} = SCALAR-STEPS {{.*}}, ir<1>, {{.*}}
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %iv = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
+  %rdx = phi i32 [ 0, %entry ], [ %rdx.next, %loop ]
+  %l = load i32, ptr %iv, align 1
+  %1 = and i32 %l, 1
+  %rdx.next = or i32 %rdx, %1
+  %iv.next = getelementptr i8, ptr %iv, i64 1
+  %ec = icmp ult ptr %iv, %end
+  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret i32 %rdx.next
+}
+
+define void @scalar_steps_first_lane_only(ptr %a, ptr %b, ptr %c) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: LV: Checking a loop in 'scalar_steps_first_lane_only'
+; CHECK: Cost of 0 for VF 2: {{.*}} = SCALAR-STEPS {{.*}}, ir<1>, {{.*}}
+; CHECK: Cost of 0 for VF 4: {{.*}} = SCALAR-STEPS {{.*}}, ir<1>, {{.*}}
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop ]
+  %gep1 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %b, i64 %iv
+  %ld1 = load i32, ptr %gep1
+  %gep2 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %c, i64 %iv
+  %ld2 = load i32, ptr %gep2
+  %add = add nsw i32 %ld2, %ld1
+  %gep3 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %a, i64 %iv
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep3
+  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, 1
+  %iv.trunc = trunc i64 %iv.next to i32
+  %exitcond = icmp eq i32 %iv.trunc, 128
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %exit, label %loop
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}
+

Summary: This commit changes InstCombine's handling of alignment operand bundles on llvm.assume calls. When an alignment assumption is attached to a GEP whose maximum preserved alignment is at least the assumed alignment, InstCombine now creates an equivalent alignment assumption on the GEP base pointer and removes the original bundle. It also adjusts preserved-alignment offset handling for wide indices and makes IRBuilder emit alignment-bundle constants as i64.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]

Summary: This commit extends SimpleLoopUnswitch's trivial-branch handling to recognize an invariant conditional whose one successor is the loop latch and whose other successor remains in the loop. For eligible finite loops with a unique latch-exit and invariant exit PHIs, it rewires the latch-directed edge to the unique latch-exit, adjusts predecessor/PHI state, updates MemorySSA or the dominator tree, and then permits the existing trivial-unswitch path to continue.
Changed symbols: unswitchTrivialBranch; SimpleLoopUnswitchPass; MemorySSAUpdater::applyUpdates; Loop::getLoopLatch; Loop::getUniqueLatchExitBlock; areLoopExitPHIsLoopInvariant
Behavioral change: Adds a new trivial-unswitch normalization for a loop-invariant branch that targets the loop latch on one arm and another in-loop block on the other arm.; Replaces the branch-to-latch CFG edge with an edge to the unique latch-exit after checking finite-loop information, loop-exit PHI invariance, and absence of side effects in the latch.; Calls LoopLatch::removePredecessor, adds equivalent incoming values to latch-exit PHIs for the rewritten predecessor, and submits Delete/Insert CFG updates through MSSAU->applyUpdates when MemorySSA is available.; Avoids repeating the later loop-exit-PHI-invariance rejection when this new branch rewrite has already established ModifiedBranch.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups assertion: "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses"; llvm::MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; llvm::SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run; simple-loop-unswitch; loop-mssa
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces under -O3 during optimizer MemorySSA maintenance.; The added tests explicitly run simple-loop-unswitch under loop-mssa and include loops containing loads and stores, including a nested-loop latch-guard case.

@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:

top_candidates.subject: [HotColdSplit] Do not add cold attribute to unchanged functions (#204003)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes HotColdSplitting so that functions detected as inherently cold are no longer marked cold/minsize merely because of that classification when the pass otherwise leaves them unchanged. The associated tests are updated to expect unchanged functions not to acquire cold attributes or outlined cold clones.
Changed symbols: HotColdSplitting::run; HotColdSplitting::isFunctionCold; markFunctionCold
Behavioral change: Stops the prior unconditional markFunctionCold-style behavior for functions identified as inherently cold but not otherwise transformed by HotColdSplitting.; Prevents unchanged functions from gaining the Cold and MinSize function attributes solely from hot/cold classification.; Leaves cold classification itself intact: isFunctionCold still recognizes an existing cold attribute, cold calling convention, or profile-based cold entry.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks
Reproducer link: The issue is an -O3 crash while updating MemorySSA.; The retrieved HotColdSplit tests concern attribute preservation and suppression of cold outlining, not a MemorySSA assertion or the reduced crash testcase.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/IPO/HotColdSplitting.cpp; HotColdSplitting; function cold/minsize attributes
Causal explanation: The change affects function attributes and whether HotColdSplitting treats unchanged cold functions as modified; it does not edit MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, loop CFG rewriting, block deletion, or SimpleLoopUnswitch. Attribute changes can indirectly alter later optimization choices, but the supplied crash trace places the failure in SimpleLoopUnswitch and MemorySSAUpdater, with no HotColdSplitting frame or pass token. The retrieved evidence therefore supports only a remote pipeline-shaping connection, not a direct cause.

top_candidates.subject: [SimplifyCFG] Use context instruction in foldBranchToCommonDest() (#203516)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Changes SimplifyCFG's foldBranchToCommonDest legality check to pass an insertion-context instruction and AssumptionCache to isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute. The context is the sole predecessor's terminator when there is exactly one predecessor, allowing the check to use assumptions valid at the point where speculated instructions will be inserted; otherwise no context is supplied. The commit threads AssumptionCache through the foldBranchToCommonDest API and adds tests covering dereferenceability supplied by attributes and assumes.
Changed symbols: llvm::foldBranchToCommonDest; SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch; isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute; AssumptionCache; load_derefable; load_derefable_assume; load_derefable_assume_var
Behavioral change: foldBranchToCommonDest now computes a context instruction from the unique predecessor terminator and passes that context plus AssumptionCache to isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute.; The branch-folding transform can treat instructions such as loads as safe to speculate when dereferenceability is established at the predecessor insertion point by an attribute or applicable llvm.assume.; For multiple predecessors, the context remains null, preserving the conservative no-single-insertion-context case.; The SimplifyCFGOpt call shown in the hunk still invokes foldBranchToCommonDest with MSSAU set to null.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA::removeFromLookups; MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run; simplifycfg
Reproducer link: The failure occurs under Clang -O3, whose recorded pass list includes simplifycfg.; The new tests show branch folding/speculation of a load based on dereferenceable information, not the reported MemorySSA assertion or a loop-unswitch reproducer.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; LLVM Transforms/Utils CFG folding; MemorySSAUpdater/SimpleLoopUnswitch in the crash trace
Causal explanation: This is a more plausible indirect candidate than a target-only InstCombine fold because it changes a generic CFG transformation in an -O3 pass listed by the crash signal. Altering whether branch folding/speculation occurs can change later CFG and loop shape, which can in turn affect downstream MemorySSA users. However, the retrieved hunks do not perform MemorySSA maintenance, do not call removeBlocks, and explicitly pass a null MSSAU in the displayed SimplifyCFGOpt call. The observed assertion is specifically during SimpleLoopUnswitch block removal, so the evidence supports only an indirect and weak-to-moderate causal link, not a demonstrated violation.

steps.subject: [SimplifyCFG] Use context instruction in foldBranchToCommonDest() (#203516)

evidence: Changes SimplifyCFG branch-folding and speculative-load legality, which can alter later CFG and loop inputs.
Visible SimplifyCFG path passes no MSSA updater and does not itself implement the failing block-removal operation.
features: assumption-aware-speculation, branch-folding, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/include/llvm/Transforms, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils, path:llvm/test/Transforms/SimplifyCFG
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This changes SimplifyCFG's foldBranchToCommonDest() speculation-safety decision to evaluate candidate instructions in the context of the predecessor terminator when there is exactly one predecessor, and to use AssumptionCache information. The foldBranchToCommonDest API is extended with an optional AssumptionCache parameter, and SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch passes Options.AC to it. New tests cover speculative load hoisting enabled by dereferenceable attributes or llvm.assume dereferenceability facts, while retaining conservative behavior for non-constant assumption sizes and multi-predecessor cases.
Changed symbols: llvm::foldBranchToCommonDest; SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch; isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute; AssumptionCache; llvm/include/llvm/Transforms/Utils/Local.h::foldBranchToCommonDest
Behavioral change: Speculation legality in foldBranchToCommonDest now receives a context instruction representing the predecessor terminator when the predecessor count is one.; Speculation legality now receives AssumptionCache, allowing dereferenceability facts from assumptions to make a load safe to speculate.; The transformation remains conservative when there is more than one predecessor by passing a null context instruction.
Assertion or trace link: The issue asserts in MemorySSA::removeFromLookups and the trace includes MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks; neither symbol is changed or called in the visible hunks.
Reproducer link: The added tests exercise speculative movement of loads under dereferenceable attributes and llvm.assume facts, not the reported reduced C reproducer or a MemorySSA assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; The O3 pass tokens include simplifycfg, but the reported failing stack is in SimpleLoopUnswitchPass and MemorySSAUpdater.
Causal explanation: This commit can change the IR shape reaching later optimization passes by allowing additional load speculation and branch folding. However, the visible call from simplifyCondBranch explicitly passes MSSAU as null, and no visible hunk updates MemorySSA, removes blocks, or invokes MemorySSAUpdater. The evidence therefore supports only an indirect and weak path to the later MemorySSA removal assertion, not a direct updater-invariant violation.
Causal confidence: 0.14
Build risk: The LLVM_ABI declaration of foldBranchToCommonDest changes signature, although the new AssumptionCache parameter has a default value.; The visible SimplifyCFG caller and implementation are updated consistently.; New transform tests cover the intended dereferenceability- and assumption-sensitive behavior.

top_candidates.subject: [AArch64] Update Cost model for CLMUL (#202965)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds AArch64 TargetTransformInfo cost modeling for llvm.clmul across NEON, AES, SVE/SVE-AES, SVE2, and SME configurations. The commit adds fixed and scalable cost-model tests and changes the expected LoopVectorize output for an AArch64 CLMUL loop, including lowering its vectorization minimum-trip-count check from 6 to 4.
Changed symbols: llvm::AArch64TTIImpl::getIntrinsicInstrCost; Intrinsic::clmul; llvm/test/Analysis/CostModel/AArch64/clmul-fixed.ll:clmul_fixed; llvm/test/Analysis/CostModel/AArch64/clmul-scalable.ll:clmul_scalable; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/clmul.ll:clmul_loop
Behavioral change: Introduces explicit AArch64 cost estimates for clmul based on legalized result type and available NEON, AES, SVE, SVE-AES, SVE2, or SME features.; Makes vectorized CLMUL comparatively cheaper for supported AArch64 feature sets, changing LoopVectorize profitability/output expectations.; Changes the tested clmul_loop vectorization threshold from n < 6 to n < 4, allowing vectorization at smaller trip counts in that target-specific case.
Assertion or trace link: The reported assertion is in MemorySSA::removeFromLookups and the stack includes MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks and SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run.; No retrieved implementation hunk references MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, removeBlocks, removeFromLookups, or SimpleLoopUnswitch.
Reproducer link: The issue reproduces during -O3 compilation, while this commit can affect optimization profitability on AArch64.; No retrieved evidence establishes that the reduced C testcase targets AArch64, contains llvm.clmul, or enters the changed LoopVectorize profitability path.
Pass or subsystem link: AArch64 TargetTransformInfo; LoopVectorize; MemorySSA/MemorySSAUpdater; SimpleLoopUnswitch
Causal explanation: The change can alter whether a specific AArch64 CLMUL loop is vectorized and thus can change later memory-IR shape. However, it is target- and intrinsic-specific cost modeling rather than a MemorySSA or CFG-update change. The observed failure is in MemorySSA removal during SimpleLoopUnswitch, and the retrieved hunks provide no bridge from CLMUL vectorization to that failing removal path. This is therefore a very weak indirect candidate.
Causal confidence: 0.04
Build risk: Adds AArch64 cost-model coverage for fixed and scalable clmul forms across feature configurations.; Updates an AArch64 LoopVectorize output test to reflect changed profitability.; No MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, SimpleLoopUnswitch, or reduced-crash-reproducer coverage is added.; The implementation is isolated to AArch64 TargetTransformInfo cost calculation and does not visibly alter generic optimizer infrastructure.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: Adds an InstCombine transform in InstCombinerImpl::commonIDivTransforms that rewrites signed or unsigned division by a one-use select containing a divisor of 1 into a select whose non-1 arm performs the division. The implementation restricts signed division to safe nonzero, non--1 constants and unsigned division to known-nonzero, non-poison divisors; accompanying div.ll tests cover successful rewrites and safety/profitability exclusions.
Changed symbols: llvm::InstCombinerImpl::commonIDivTransforms; llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/div.ll:sdiv_select_one_false; llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/div.ll:sdiv_select_one_true; llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/div.ll:udiv_select_one_false; llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine/div.ll:udiv_select_one_false_nonnull_var
Behavioral change: Replaces X / (select Cond, 1, Y) with select Cond, X, (X / Y), and analogously handles the select form with 1 in the false arm.; Creates a new division in one select arm and returns a newly created select at the original select's insertion point.; Avoids the rewrite for signed divisors that are zero or -1, for unsigned divisors not proven nonzero and non-poison, and when the original select has multiple uses.
Assertion or trace link: The failing pipeline includes instcombine.; The reported assertion is MemorySSA::removeFromLookups: MA->use_empty() && "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses".; The supplied stack identifies MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks and SimpleLoopUnswitchPass::run, not InstCombine.
Reproducer link: Both the issue and this candidate concern transformations reachable under -O3.; No retrieved hunk contains the reduced C reproducer, MemorySSA access creation/removal, or an assertion test.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; MemorySSA/MemorySSAUpdater; SimpleLoopUnswitch
Causal explanation: This is an O3-reachable InstCombine IR rewrite and can change later optimization input, but the shown rewrite only manipulates pure integer division and select instructions. It neither changes control-flow blocks nor updates MemorySSA, and the crash stack points to MemorySSA block removal during SimpleLoopUnswitch. The retrieved evidence therefore supports only an indirect, weak possibility that altered IR later exposes the MemorySSA bug, not a direct causal mechanism.
Causal confidence: 0.13
Build risk: Implementation change is covered by added InstCombine div.ll tests, including negative safety cases.; No MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, loop-unswitch, or crash-reproducer test is added.; The change is localized to InstCombine and introduces no visible build-system or API changes.

top_candidates.subject: [AssumeBundleQueries] Use correct default value for dereferenceable (#203943)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit corrects how llvm::getKnowledgeFromBundle assigns default argument values for assume operand bundles. It replaces a universal default of 1 with attribute-specific defaults: alignment defaults to 1, while dereferenceable and dereferenceable_or_null default to 0. Tests show that a concrete dereferenceable size of 1 permits SimplifyCFG load speculation, whereas an unknown size is no longer treated as sufficient proof for that speculation.
Changed symbols: llvm::getKnowledgeFromBundle; GetArgOr; align_deref_size_1; align_deref_size_unknown
Behavioral change: The local bundle-argument helper now accepts an explicit default rather than always returning 1 for a missing/nonconstant argument.; Alignment bundle knowledge retains a default value of 1, including the secondary alignment operand passed through MinAlign.; Dereferenceable and dereferenceable_or_null bundle knowledge now defaults to 0 instead of 1.; Consumers such as SimplifyCFG no longer infer one byte of dereferenceability from an unknown or unavailable dereferenceable-size argument; the added test expects no speculative load hoist for a runtime-unknown size.
Assertion or trace link: The crash assertion is MemorySSA::removeFromLookups with a live MemoryAccess, reached from MemorySSAUpdater::removeBlocks and SimpleLoopUnswitchPass.; No retrieved hunk changes MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, removeBlocks, SimpleLoopUnswitch, or removeFromLookups.; The -O3 trace includes simplifycfg, and this commit adds SimplifyCFG tests, but the reported failing stack identifies loop unswitching rather than SimplifyCFG.
Reproducer link: The added reproducer-style tests concern llvm.assume dereferenceable bundles and conditional-load speculation.; No retrieved evidence establishes that the reduced C testcase contains such assume bundles, dereferenceability facts, or the tested speculative-load pattern.
Pass or subsystem link: AssumeBundleQueries analysis; SimplifyCFG speculative dereferenceable-load transformation; MemorySSA failure during SimpleLoopUnswitch
Causal explanation: The change can alter optimizer decisions by making dereferenceability knowledge more conservative, thereby changing whether SimplifyCFG speculates and hoists loads. Such altered IR could indirectly affect later optimization inputs, but the evidence does not show a path from this assume-bundle query to the MemorySSAUpdater block-removal assertion, nor does it show that the failing testcase uses the affected bundle form. This is therefore only an indirect subsystem-level connection.
Causal confidence: 0.10
Build risk: Implementation change is limited to llvm/lib/Analysis/AssumeBundleQueries.cpp.; New llvm/test/Transforms/SimplifyCFG/speculate-derefable-load.ll coverage distinguishes constant size 1 from an unknown size.; The behavioral correction may change optimization results for IR using dereferenceable assume bundles, but no direct MemorySSA test is included.
